comments.author: @trevorharley4475
comments.text: I bought a new Nissan titan in 2024. Sticker was 59 grand. Never pay sticker. I paid 50 with 2 grand down. 0% financing. The truck is now two years old. Valued at 41k trade in value and I owe 32k. I may be one of 17 people in the country with positive equity in my auto loan. They payments are steep at 900 a month but at least I can sell it, pay it off and walk away with cash in hand. My point is I'm not the smartest man on earth and I was able to do basic math and read paperwork before signing. Don't look at the monthly payment alone. Look at depreciation, actual market value, interest (that's the big one) and never trust the guy trying to sell you something. I've worked at dealerships. They can get you in the car you want and the payment you want, that's easy. What you don't see is its 18% interest on an 84 month loan. Just because the payments are where you want them does not mean you can afford it!

Two thought from a random youtube guy: I have a special ordered Bronco Sasquatch. MSRP was $62500 because it has close to $20,000 in factory options. Not dealer stuff. Factory stuff. I need a truck now. Dealers are offering me $31,000-$39,000. I didnt roll anything into the bronco, I had equity in my truck. Moral of this story is...you never got a good deal. You think you did but you didnt.

Second, while shopping for a truck I started with new vehicles because of the insane rebates and interest rates. Those two things don't go together though. First off, I was looking at a Ram Big Horn. I have had two of these and a Rebel. Ram has been putting out trash. They are up to their eyeballs in 2025 and 2026 trucks. No one wanted their stupid hurricane motor. They brought back the hemi. These trucks are so insanely overpriced it is ridiculous and of course they tried to stick me with $2,800 worth of non sense like the "desert protection" and "Nitrogen filled tires." I told them I wasnt paying for that and to let the nitrogen out of the tires and fill them back up with regular air. Anyway...I have insane credit, 796-815. My wife and I make plenty of money. In order to get a decent price on the new Rams you have to take all the rebates but then the interest rate goes from 0% for 60 months to 5.9% for 84 months. Even with either deal, the interest rate or the rebate my payment was close to 900 for the lowest model big horn or highest model express. I wanted another Rebel, not touching that for under $900 a month. I am not talking about all of you wealthy youtubers with $50,000 down. I am talking about an average moron like me, with a small amount of negative equity with good credit that doesn't want to pay $900 a month for a vehicle that should have been about $40k out the door. 

Ram dealers are out of their damn minds with this BS. Don't get me started on Ford....Chevy had the best prices but that truck is a stripped down truck that looks like it is from the early 2000's not current. For reference, I am in Las Vegas and I talked to every Ram dealer in the city and two of the Ford dealers. Chevy was not getting me in the door with those stripped down trucks.
